senses.definition: The name of the Latin script letter T/t.
examples: ETA [is spoken] as "ee-tee-ay" instead of "I SPELL Echo Tango Alfa".

quotes.text: The word length, which contains only four sounds l e ng th, is usually spell'd thus, el ee en gee tee aitch.
quotes.reference: 1773 October, The Monthly Review Or Literary Journal Enlarged:

quotes.text: They have writing samples and examine the back loops of pees and the crosses of tees.

senses.definition: Something shaped like the letter T.

examples: Brendan pulled a black tee over his head.

senses.definition: (computing) The process of redirecting output to multiple destinations.
(computing) To redirect output to multiple destinations.

quotes.text: […] teeing via multiple redirects (ls > file1 > file2) […]

senses.definition: (golf) A flat area of ground from which players hit their first shots on a golf hole.
(sports) A usually wooden or plastic peg from which a ball is kicked or hit.

quotes.text: Pollard, who went into the semifinals with an unsatisfactory 63% return from the kicking tee, turned it around splendidly against Wales and he continued that form despite missing his first attempt in the final.
quotes.reference: 2019 November 3, Liam de Carme, “Boks, you beauties”, in Sunday Times:

senses.definition: (curling) The target area of a curling rink.
The mark at which players aim in quoits.
(golf) To place a ball on a tee

quotes.text: If at any hole a competitor play his first stroke from outside the limits of the teeing-ground, he shall count that stroke, tee a ball, and play his second stroke from within these limits.

senses.definition: (obsolete) To teach, educate, train, bring up.
A finial resembling an umbrella, crowning a dagoba in Indochinese countries.
